scenario: [LNUL.4.1] and [LREG.1.3]: a regex match on an absent string propagates `null`, so the activation continues for neither `~` nor `!~`. `msg` is `String?`, which keeps both matches beta join tests through `FN_REGEX_MATCH` (a decided match on a non-nullable slot is an alpha REGEX test instead; RLOW.5.2.2). With `msg` absent neither `match` nor `no_match` fires, and no TypeError is raised: `saw_type_error` matches any `TypeError` fault fact ([LERR.9.3]) and must never fire. With `msg` "abc", which `/x/` does not match, only `no_match` fires. A runtime that treated `null !~ /x/` as a non-match fires `no_match` twice and fails here. PATH PINNED: `FN_REGEX_MATCH` over a `null` subject, and the `!~` negation over its result -- libds `builtin_regex_match` (builtins.c) through rete/eval.c, Mercury `ds.eval`'s `fn_regex_match` arm.
rules_ds:
schema L scope logical:
    id: Int key
    msg: String? mutable

rule match:
    L l where l.msg ~ /x/
->
    log info "match"

rule no_match:
    L l where l.msg !~ /x/
->
    log info "no match"

rule saw_type_error:
    TypeError
->
    log critical "type error"
